claims.text: An ultrathin tungsten interlayer can be used to induce a transition from diffusion-mediated to dislocation-mediated creep in HEA multilayers.
Adding an ultrathin tungsten interlayer promotes interface coherency in HEA multilayers.
The proposed initial material consists of conventional HEA multilayers without a dedicated interfacial transition layer.
The tungsten layer is incorporated at the interfaces between HEA layers.
Both diffusion creep and dislocation creep can be active under the proposed high-temperature testing conditions.
A tungsten interlayer reduces lattice misfit at HEA multilayer interfaces.
A tungsten interlayer limits fast diffusion paths at HEA multilayer interfaces.
Improved interface coherency restricts atomic diffusion along interfacial boundaries.
Restricting interfacial diffusion suppresses diffusion-mediated creep.
Suppressing diffusion-mediated creep makes dislocation nucleation and glide the dominant creep mechanism.
Tungsten-modified HEA multilayers will exhibit a lower diffusion-associated creep rate than unmodified multilayers.
Tungsten-modified HEA multilayers will exhibit dislocation activity such as pile-ups or slip bands.
Unmodified HEA multilayers are dominated by diffusion-mediated creep at comparable temperatures and stresses.
The proposed effect exists only within a particular tungsten-interlayer thickness and deposition-quality range.
The creep-mechanism transition is sensitive to testing temperature and applied stress.
